wiki.tagline: Turn a codebase you don't know into a clear, readable wiki.
wiki.when: You've joined a new repo, you're documenting a project, or you want teammates to onboard by reading instead of asking around.
example: Open the repo you want documented, load this kit, and start a new chat.
Say: "Onboard this codebase and write a wiki to docs/."
codebase-onboarding maps the tech stack, the entry points, and the folder structure.
repo-scan inventories the files, and code-tour walks you through the important paths.
architecture and architecture-decision-records capture how it's built and why those choices were made.
documentation and docs-page turn all of that into linked Markdown pages; knowledge-ops keeps them organized.
You end up with a docs/ wiki a new teammate can read start to finish.
tips: Load the kit, then start a fresh chat so the skills come online.
Point Bob at the actual repo folder before you ask.
Ask for it 'written to docs/' so you get real files, not just a chat answer.

product-frameworks.tagline: The three PM thinking frameworks most tools skip: why users come (Jobs to Be Done), why they stay (Hook Model), and why they convert (CRO).
product-frameworks.when: Retention or growth is the problem — people try the product but don't stick, or don't convert — and you want discovery rooted in real motivation, not feature requests.
example: Start with jobs-to-be-done: run switch interviews to find the real job and, crucially, the ANXIETY blocking the switch.
Use opportunity-solution-tree to map that job to a few solution bets instead of jumping to features.
Apply hook-model to design the return loop: internal trigger -> easy action -> variable reward -> investment. Run the ethics gate before shipping.
At first-use or the paywall, use cro-objections: list the 5 doubts a real visitor has and answer each with evidence, in their own words.
Prove it with cohort-analysis: does the retention curve flatten? That's the number that says the loop works.
value-proposition and north-star-metric keep the story and the one metric honest throughout.
tips: Write the job solution-free (verb + object + context) before proposing anything.
Design the INTERNAL trigger first — an external notification alone never forms a habit.
In cro-objections, use the customer's exact words; matching their language is what converts.
Pick ONE north-star (return rate, not signups) so retention work has a scoreboard.

pm-methodology.tagline: Take a product idea from a blank page to shipped, measured, and iterated — one anchor skill per phase.
pm-methodology.when: You want a repeatable process instead of ad-hoc PM work, or you are onboarding to a structured product lifecycle.
example: Foundation: foundation-lean-canvas — capture the bet on one page (problem, users, value, the one metric).
Discover: discover-interview-synthesis — turn raw interviews into patterns and real needs.
Define: define-jtbd-canvas — frame the job the product is hired to do.
Develop: develop-solution-brief — shape the solution and its rationale before building.
Deliver: deliver-prd — write the PRD and hand off to build.
Measure: measure-experiment-design — design the experiment that tells you if it worked.
Iterate: iterate-retrospective — capture what you learned and decide the next move.
tips: Run the phases in order — each phase feeds the next.
This kit is the spine; the full product-on-purpose set has more skills per phase (discover-market-sizing, deliver-user-stories, measure-experiment-results) when you need depth.
Pair with the product-frameworks kit for the JTBD / Hook / CRO thinking behind the phases.

software-development.tagline: Ship code a senior would approve — test-first, your stack's patterns, nothing over-built.
software-development.when: Building or refactoring a feature you'll have to maintain.
example: Say what you're building. It writes the failing test first, then the code (tdd-workflow).
It applies your stack's patterns (python / react / go / fastapi / django) and shapes the API and system design.
ponytail and karpathy-guidelines cut over-engineering and the usual LLM slips.
It runs the checks before it calls anything done.
tips: Name your stack.
It won't claim 'verified' without running the check.

data-analysis.tagline: Analyze data and grade AI output without fooling yourself.
data-analysis.when: Doing analytics, or measuring how good an AI pipeline actually is.
example: error-analysis reads real traces and names the failure modes before you count anything.
write-judge-prompt builds a Pass/Fail evaluator for the subjective calls.
validate-evaluator calibrates that judge against human labels.
SQL and statistics do the numbers.
tips: An uncalibrated judge is a random number.
Score retrieval and answer separately.

product-management.tagline: From fuzzy idea to shipped, measured feature — the whole PM toolkit.
product-management.when: Planning and strategy, not code: PRDs, roadmaps, prioritization, go-to-market.
example: jobs-to-be-done finds the real need behind the ask.
create-prd and user-stories spec it.
prioritization-frameworks (RICE) ranks what's worth building.
north-star-metric and gtm-strategy ship and measure it.
tips: Describe the situation, not the skills.
Pair with pm-methodology (process) and product-frameworks (thinking).

production-engineering.tagline: Design, ship, and run production systems — past 'works on my laptop'.
production-engineering.when: Deploying, operating, or hardening real infrastructure.
example: system-design and deployment-patterns shape it for production.
docker / kubernetes / terraform ship it.
runbook and incident-response for when it breaks at 3am.
tips: Write the runbook before you need it.
For a specific prod bug, add the bug-fixing kit.

test-engineering.tagline: Tests that actually catch regressions — unit, end-to-end, and back.
test-engineering.when: Writing or hardening a suite you'll trust to gate a release.
example: testing-strategy decides what to test at each level, and what to skip.
It writes the unit, end-to-end, and regression tests.
verification-before-completion, so green means green.
tips: Test behavior, not implementation.
A test that can't fail tests nothing.

application-security.tagline: Break it like an attacker, then write code that resists — audit to fix.
application-security.when: Running an audit or pen-test, or hardening a feature before ship.
example: bb-methodology scopes and plans the hunt.
The hunt-* skills work each class: xss, sqli, ssrf, idor, auth-bypass.
vibesec prevents them at write-time, not just finds them.
You get a clean, reproducible report.
tips: hunt-* finds; vibesec prevents.
Reproduce every finding before reporting it.

frontend-design.tagline: Interfaces people enjoy — polished, accessible, and alive.
example: frontend-design lays out the structure.
design-system and frontend patterns keep it consistent.
motion gives it feel; fixing-accessibility makes it usable by everyone.
tips: Accessibility isn't a phase — bake it in.
Motion should guide, not perform.

web-research.tagline: A synthesized answer with sources — not 40 open tabs.
web-research.when: You need to understand something you don't yet know.
example: deep-research plans what to look for and why.
exa-search and x-research gather the material.
research-synthesis turns it into an answer you can cite.
tips: Ask for sources so you can check the claims.
search-first before answering from memory.

release-review.tagline: The last gate before ship — catch what a tired reviewer misses.
release-review.when: Right before a merge or release.
example: code-review across correctness, security, simplicity, and tests.
security-audit, plus a check that tests cover the change.
verification-before-completion and karpathy-guidelines for the common slips.
tips: Run it before you merge, not after.
One confirmed blocker beats ten vague nits.

bug-fixing.tagline: Root cause, not symptom — fixed fast.
bug-fixing.when: Something's broken and you need it working now.
example: Reproduce, then systematic-debugging isolates the real cause.
Stuck? caveman-debug drops in prints to see what's actually happening.
error-handling fixes it properly — no silent catch.
tips: Reproduce before you fix.
Fix the cause, not the log line.

code-simplification.tagline: Delete the over-engineering — the best code is the code you didn't write.
code-simplification.when: A diff or repo feels bloated and you want it lean.
example: ponytail-review reads the diff and ranks what to cut.
ponytail-audit finds bloat across the whole repo.
It keeps the laziest working solution: stdlib before custom, one line before fifty.
tips: Eight sharp lines beat fifty clever ones.
Delete first; add back only what you miss.

rag-evaluation.tagline: Prove your RAG works — retrieval and answer, scored apart.
rag-evaluation.when: Measuring or improving a retrieval / RAG agent.
example: evaluate-rag scores retrieval quality and answer quality separately.
error-analysis finds the pattern in the failures.
write-judge-prompt and validate-evaluator give you a judge you've calibrated.
tips: Never trust an uncalibrated judge.
Bad retrieval and bad generation are different bugs.

content-writing.tagline: Docs and copy that sound human — not AI.
content-writing.when: Writing docs or copy, or cleaning up a draft.
example: draft-content or copywriting for the first pass.
no-ai-slop strips the AI tells while keeping your voice.
ux-copy and brand-voice set the tone; seo if it's for search.
tips: Run no-ai-slop after drafting, not instead of it.
Match the brand voice — generic copy converts no one.
